note: Geometry for the supplements Shorts (long-form 03). Source is OUR OWN clean cut - one locked kitchen camera, no burned graphics anywhere - so unlike the ab-wheel batch there are no cards, no pips and nothing to avoid slicing. Every shot is a full-bleed 9:16 talk crop. All numbers below are measured off full-resolution frames with Apple Vision, not estimated.

talk.note: MEASURED, and it is not the ab-wheel's 724x1080. Dan stands behind a counter with ~180 source rows of dead kitchen ceiling above his head, so a full-height window spends a quarter of the Short on ceiling and leaves him small. Cropping 120 rows off the TOP narrows the window (fixed 2:3 aspect - the skill's trap, and here it is the right direction) and makes him bigger. 644x960 -> 1080x1610 is 1.68x, against 1.78x for the V2/V3 full-height 9:16 crops, so it is also SHARPER than those. His head then lands at delivered y=406, 96px clear of the title band; the next step down (cropTop 140) gives only 63px and was rejected as too tight against 6-frames-per-beat sampling.
talk.agNote: The AG1 bag sits at x 0.804-0.964 with its printed logo at 0.804-0.946, so EVERY window centred on Dan (torso 0.668-0.697) cuts through the print. Both fixes were measured and both are worse: including the whole bag needs centre 0.776, putting him 255px off centre in the delivered frame, and excluding it needs centre 0.616, putting him 206px off with a dead dark cabinet filling the left third - which is exactly the fault Dan flagged on v2-short3 at 133px. A partly-visible product on a real counter is set dressing, not a sliced editorial graphic; the centring rule wins. Rendered and reviewed before committing.
talk.tightNote: PUNCH-IN, added rev 2. Dan flagged four 'awkward cut' / 'jump cut' timecodes; all four are picture cuts inherited from the source edit, which joins 62 takes of the same locked camera. Measured, a naked one scores 7.64 mean-abs-difference against a 1.30 adjacent-frame baseline - and REMOVING A PAUSE scores 4.97-12.46, i.e. as bad or worse, because he moves while he is not talking. So a join cannot simply be made; it has to be HIDDEN. Every join now alternates wide/tight, which reads as a camera change instead of a glitch and is the same fix the spray-tan longform used on 35 of its 43 joins. 578x862 -> 1080x1610 is 1.87x against the wide shot's 1.68x; top 126 keeps his head at the same delivered y (410) so only the FRAMING changes, not his position in frame.

card.note: Unused in this batch - the clean master carries no graphics to preserve.

audio.note: ⚠ UNLIKE THE AB-WHEEL BATCH, THIS SOURCE HAS NO MUSIC BED - the 8/27 rebuild added inserts, not a bed, and the style gate's bed check reads 0.8-1.1x on videos that carry none. So there is no bar to drop into and no bed to stop dead, and the fades are short: just enough to keep a splice from ticking. Durations are preserved exactly (no acrossfade), so picture and sound stay frame-locked.

dropNote: STANDING RULE (Dan, 2026-08-28): the title must never sit on his face or his abs. 'move me down or if not possible move title to bottom of captions.' On a full-bleed 9:16 crop there is no vertical slack - his head starts at source row 35, i.e. y62 in the delivered frame, and a 2-line Impact headline runs to y300 - so the picture is DROPPED to start at y=310 and the J2 field carries the title above it. Measured: his head then starts at y362, clear by 62px. Costs 16% of picture height and BUYS sharpness - the source crop widens from 608 to 724, so the upscale falls from 1.78x to 1.49x. Cards are unaffected: their stage top is y170 and the title only ever overlaps the sky at the top of a card.
titleScrimNote: The scrim ends exactly where the dropped picture starts, so it can never reach the picture. It still earns its place on CARD shots, whose stage top is y170 - there the title crosses the top of the card, which is sky.
titleNote: STANDING RULE (Dan, 2026-08-28): the title holds for the WHOLE short, on the black field only, never over the picture. The picture is dropped to y=310 to make room. Supersedes the V4-era 'title must not stay up the whole video' rule, which was written when the title sat on his face.
